Fastmail's developer page documents JMAP's machine-readable discovery model: "The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session" (the session object advertises capabilities, accounts, and API URLs; /.well-known/jmap answers with the standard RFC 8620 redirect), with CORS-enabled APIs and API-token auth. "The full API specification documents" are the IETF RFCs (8620, 8621, 9610); this is authenticated per-account runtime discovery, not a downloadable OpenAPI-style spec file, and no OpenAPI exists on fastmail.com.
Fastmail is fantastic, I've been a very happy customer for at least a couple years now. Masked emails have been so nice for throwaway/sketchy sites. It's done everything I could ask.

Fastmail is the service I've paid for longer than any other, without any pauses, and with the most satisfaction of any subscription... it works perfectly for me and offers excellent value for what I pay. It's so gratifyingly functional and boring.
Been about 10 years now and it is the definition of 'It just works'. I like that they are up front with how the data is handled and what that can mean for privacy.
As an alternative to forwarding, you can configure Fastmail to fetch mail from (and send via) Gmail like a mail client.

Uses a Google Workspace account for their custom domain while email for that domain stays at Fastmail, and it works fine. The only hassle is the calendar: you can add your Fastmail calendar to Google Calendar, but Google is slow to sync.
Migration workflow: set up a filter on Fastmail showing all mail delivered to the old @gmail.com address in the last two weeks, then periodically went through it to unsubscribe or change addresses.

Switching is an easy process these days, just insanely time consuming. Fastmail has an easy migration tool if you don't want to go the IMAP route. Migrating filters and rules over, on the other hand...

Uses Fastmail SMTP for transactional emails with an app password that can only access SMTP. Fastmail isn't really intended for this since the limits don't scale to large services, but it works well enough.
Switched from ProtonMail to Fastmail recently. Fastmail was a ton faster and didn't randomly forget my sessions. Night and day to use. It also let me use two custom domains without paying twice.

Switched primary email to Fastmail a few months ago. Wanted something that works well, is paid with proper support, allows custom domains, and is cheapest. Fastmail fit the bill and is working as expected.

Used Fastmail as part of a DeGoogle effort and is very happy with it; mail gets delivered to recipients' inboxes. However, as an Australian service it raises privacy/five-eyes concerns, a price they accepted because business mail must arrive.
Loved the product and the company but left because they couldn't accept data being under both Australian and American jurisdictions; says privacy claims are aspirational given hosting locations.
Was very pleasantly surprised how easy the move from Google services to Fastmail was (with domain managed by Cloudflare).
On spam filtering: 'Actually really good. I've just checked my spam folder and it's full - nothing has made it through.' Another user: 'I pretty much never see spam.'

Criticism of Fastmail's new EU (Amsterdam) region: they state they can't guarantee data remains only in the EU, so commenters say businesses with strict data-residency requirements won't touch it and it misses why people want EU hosting.
Recently moved email to FastMail and really likes it, even preferring its web interface over Gmail's.
FastMail is an upgrade from Gmail. Good enough that after swearing never to pay for webmail, I remain a paying customer after 10+ years.

Complaint: text smileys like ':)' get replaced by yellow emoji icons (in plain-text view); support seemed uninterested in adding an option to disable it. Another user made a Stylish userstyle to hide them. Otherwise 'an excellent, excellent service.'
Critic notes that FastMail's Android app relies on Google Cloud Messaging for push, so users leaving Gmail for privacy still depend on Google for functionality.
Very happy customer for at least a couple of years. Masked emails have been great for throwaway or sketchy sites; it does everything they could ask, and they recommend it to anyone switching.

After switching 6 Gmail accounts, they were bombarded with spam Google had been catching. Constant flagging doesn't seem to help, so they built a convoluted mess of filters. They also miss Gmail's auto-categorization into primary/promotions/social/updates.

Likes Fastmail but feels the subscription is a bit overpriced for their use (IMAP only, no app, calendars, contacts or files). They found cheaper independent providers, though most likely have a low bus factor.

Subdomain addressing is a killer feature: foo@bar.mydomain.com always works where plus/dot addresses get rejected. Gmail integration for ingesting mail and calendars works fantastically. Offline mode finally arrived. The UI is still a bit clunky (email view reloads for no reason), but it's stable, fast and reliable.
Customer for about 20 years. Worst: a 2006 outage kept them from downloading homework. Best: after deleting all their emails in the 2020s through an IMAP mistake, a human contacted them and fixed it.

Moved from Fastmail to Gmail. Fastmail is excellent for explicit organisation, but its implicit organisation isn't great: they want things like package-arrival and boarding-pass summaries, which Gmail does.
Moved business email to Fastmail. Gmail's web interface is bad by comparison; Fastmail is way more responsive and fluid and feels almost native.

Former customer receiving mail via SES: the setup worked for years, then broke overnight. Support said it was a deliberate configuration change. It later started working again with no further contact from support.

Misses Gmail's automatic categorization. Fastmail filters don't apply to existing emails, which is a major hassle, so they use Sanebox despite disliking third-party access. The web interface has improved immensely.
Found a calendar UI bug; it took about 6 back-and-forths with first-line support over a week before it was (said to be) passed to developers.
When broke, they asked for a grace period on renewal; Fastmail gave them 2 months with no questions asked, and they settled up later.
Customer since 2014 and never regretted it. Loves the web interface, 2FA options and Android app. Easy account switching, family setup and custom-domain setup.
European customer who moved to Fastmail a couple of years ago: very happy so far, and the Gmail migrator works great.
Text smileys like ":)" are replaced by yellow emoji icons client-side, and support seemed uninterested in adding an option to turn it off. Otherwise an excellent service.
Business user, mostly happy, but every morning for three years has marked 10-15 messages as spam without making headway training the filter.
Switched from Gmail/Google Apps because of better web shortcuts, a good mobile web UI, better IMAP (no 15-connection limit), working CardDAV, flexible Sieve filters, folders, and subdomain aliasing.
Used Fastmail for six months then returned to Google Apps. Search was much slower, folders made organizing harder than labels, they missed Gmail's inbox categories, and more spam got through.
The Android app gives real push notifications, unlike the Gmail app on Fastmail's backend, which delayed mail up to 15 minutes. But the app's web-view interface is low-resolution and slow to load.
Worried Masked Email needed both Fastmail and 1Password, but was delighted that only Fastmail is required; it's an option in settings.
Customer for 4 years, happy with pricing and service, but plans to migrate away from Australian providers over the new anti-encryption law.
